scope: Browser window lifecycle, reliable result headings, app exit and complete radio/podcast keyboard menus.

topics.title: Radio and podcasts by keyboard and voice
details: Radio and Podcasts open shared action menus. Arrows, Home/End, first-letter navigation and Enter choose actions. Tab/Shift+Tab switches between actions and results. Result lists support the same navigation; Enter plays stations, presets, saved recordings and downloaded episodes, or opens a podcast show. Escape backs out through episodes, results, actions and the main menu. Voice Actions, Results, Next action, Previous action and spoken menu labels use the same state.

Search and browse forms accept typed or spoken values. Radio forms cover genre, country, state, city, database choice, preset naming, recording length, scheduling day/time/length/daily repeat and RadioSure import path. Podcast forms cover search/category, automatic download limits and seek amounts. Tab/Shift+Tab visits fields, OK and Cancel; Enter continues or submits, Escape cancels. Choice fields support arrows, Home/End, letters and spoken option navigation. Invalid input keeps the form open.

Ctrl+F opens search. Ctrl+P lists radio presets or podcast subscriptions. F5 refreshes station directories or subscriptions. Space pauses/resumes selected audio, Ctrl+R resumes, Ctrl+S stops and Ctrl+Left/Right seeks 15 seconds where supported. Ctrl+D saves a radio preset or downloads a selected podcast episode. Radio actions include recording, scheduling, stopping recordings and individually browsing saved recordings and schedules. Podcast actions include subscriptions, episodes, offline downloads, automatic/manual downloads, seeking and chapter/episode/show controls.

Deleting a preset, canceling a selected schedule or removing a subscription asks Yes or No. Y/N answers immediately; arrows/Tab choose and Enter confirms, Escape cancels. Schedule cancellation and subscription removal use stable identifiers so the intended item is removed. Removing a subscription does not delete existing downloaded audio.

topics.title: Keep browser window open
details: Options, Web browsing includes Keep browser window open, unchecked by default. Say Keep browser window open on or off. When off, leaving the browser activity closes all windows and tabs in Companion’s dedicated browser context. Your ordinary browser windows are unaffected.

When enabled, leaving the activity retains the browser page. Choosing Web browser from the main menu raises the retained page and refreshes Companion’s virtual reader rather than requiring another search. If the retained page has been closed, the typed/voice search prompt opens normally. Exiting Voice Companion closes its owned browser context regardless of this preference.

topics.title: Heading navigation and concise page loading
details: Repeated H and Shift+H retain the selected semantic heading when a nested link shares its text position. Caret acknowledgments and incidental DOM refreshes no longer reset the cursor into that nested link and cause repeated headings.

Result heading labels prefer the title text over URL/breadcrumb metadata. Search-result links use available title text while retaining the original DOM identity for safe activation. Page-loaded speech no longer announces heading or link totals.

Alt+F4 again requests exit of the entire app from editable text, browser reading, media menus, confirmation prompts and Options. Existing exit confirmation and unsaved-document review remain in force.

topics.title: Documentation and verification
details: The built-in Help guide and versioned What’s New formats include the new browser preference, media menus/forms, shortcuts and matching voice commands. Existing email, document, web-form review and guided voice workflows remain covered by regression tests.

Tests exercise radio/podcast keyboard and voice interchange, validation, recording/scheduling, subscriptions/download policies, confirmations, actual Windows key dispatch and browser window cleanup. Live fixtures cover nested result headings, caret updates and result activation across Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Brave. Site-specific search results, radio streams and podcast hosts still require beta testing.
